items.parsed_text: Capesize Report24th March 2026 PAC: Very Quiet ATL: Steady Market Comments A second consecutive day without majors, ensured a suitably quiet Eastern basin. Both operator C5 and peripheral demand felt moderate, whilst spot tonnage began to encroach on the lengthier side after a day of minimal activity. Charterers eager to engage, an operator kicked the day’s activity oﬀ ﬁxing their Walcott to Qingdao stem for 03-12 April dates at low $11.00’s. On the C5, $11.25 was done for 08-12 April by another operator. End April the focal point in the South, after a few charterers narrowed their focus within the 20-30 April window. Bids congregated at $30 for the back half of this window, against oﬀers closer to mid $31.00’s. Earlier dates saw oﬀers sub $31.00, however lacked stems on their dates. A relatively lacklustre day in the South overall. Transatlantic business the bulk of North Atlantic demand. Early on an operator ﬁxed their Drummond to Rotterdam stem for mid April close to the bid at $14.65 – from Gibraltar this ran to $22,300 C8 equivalent. An end-user tendered their forward Acu to Ijmuiden stem but found few candidates. They will instead search for tonnage in the market, rather than auction. items.parsed_text: Handysize/Supramax Report24th March 2026 63,500 Atlantic: SOFTER Paciﬁc: FIRMER 38,000 Atlantic: SOFTER Paciﬁc: FLAT Market Comments ATLANTIC: On the Continent, the Handysize market has seen limited change so far this week, with conditions remaining broadly stable. Rates are holding just below last done levels, with a slight softer bias, though very few ﬁxtures have been reported. A steady tonnage list and a light ﬂow of enquiry, including a few Continent to Mediterranean grain cargoes, continue to keep the market balanced. However, we have seen some softening on scrap runs, with a 35,000 deadweight vessel ﬁxing from the Continent to Turkey at USD 16,000, around USD 2,500 lower than levels seen last week, where a similar 34,000 deadweight vessel was rated in the high teens for the same route. On the Supramax and Ultramax market, the Continent has seen little change so far this week, with the softer sentiment from last week persisting. Rates are holding just below previous levels, as steady vessel supply continues to outweigh limited enquiry. We are seeing a 63,000 deadweight vessel ﬁxing a Trans-Atlantic trip at around USD 11,000, in line with levels seen at the end of last week. Overall, activity remains muted, with ongoing bunker volatility and a lack of fresh drivers keeping the market subdued. In the Mediterranean Handysize market, there has been limited change so far this week, with rates holding around last done levels. In the East Mediterranean and Black Sea, conditions remain broadly stable, with grain activity providing little fresh impetus, while more standard routes remain largely unchanged. In the West Mediterranean owners continue to favour local employment which have kept rates ﬂat. We saw a 34,000 deadweight vessel ﬁx basis Egypt for a trip to redeliver to the USEC with salt for USD 11,500 – which are the same levels seen at the end of last week. On the Supramax and Ultramax market in the Mediterranean, it has been very quiet so far this week, with little change in overall conditions. Rates are broadly in line with last done levels, with a marginal easing as demand remains thin. We have seen Trans-Atlantic trips ease by around USD 500 compared to last week, now at ﬁxing levels at approximately USD 10,000. The East Coast South America market remains very quiet today, as an oversupply of Handysize tonnage weighs on sentiment and Ultramax owners continue to oﬀer $26,000 for Transatlantic trips despite a total lack of ﬁrm bids at those levels. In the US Gulf Supramax and Ultramax market, this week we have seen more forward pricing but not a lot of action for April dates yet as the Us Gulf market drifts. Fronthaul has been concluded on an Ultra at 19k with Grains to Asia and 17k on an Ultra for grains decent duration to East Med for Early April so for now it feels steadish. In the US Gulf Handysize market, conditions are broadly ﬂat to softer, with limited cargo activity and a steadily building tonnage list. Fundamentals remain unchanged, with low cargo availability against high vessel supply continuing to pressure the market. Rates are holding around, or just below, last done levels, with ongoing bunker volatility further weighing on sentiment and limiting forward visibility. We are seeing a 38,000 deadweight vessels ﬁxing Trans-Atlantic trips at around USD 17,000, approximately USD 500 lower than levels seen at the end of last week. PACIFIC: The Paciﬁc market remained relatively quiet this week. Overall, SEA continued to feel soft, but with new cargo emerging and vessel supply in the region being limited, the market saw a slight uptick on Tuesday. It was heard that an SMX open in Singapore ﬁxed at the high-$13,000s back to China. For trip to sea can get a bit more as some owners still discount to China for dd reason. In the Far East, the market remained quiet this week also. The conclusion of the Shanghai BB Expo has not yet brought fresh vitality to the market, though cargo volumes have increased somewhat, keeping overall supply and demand balanced. Most owners still do not prefer the WCI direction. It was heard that a newbuilt ﬁxed at around mid 16k for trip to the Med via Goa. However, most charterers for bh biz still prefer via COGH considering the conﬂict in middle east and the bunker price, with rates not particularly high, oﬀering SMX vessels generally around 11500-12k levels. Nopac saw limited cargo this week, with charterers calculating UMX levels around 14500, while owners' ideas from NChina are generally around 16000. Australia was relatively more active this week compared to last, with some new cargoes emerging. Charterers calculated rates for a UMX from Singapore at around 15-16k levels for trip to China. Local cargo export volumes from WCI remain limited. South Africa overall shows no downward trend. Most cargoes are bound for India, but owners prefer to position vessels to the Paciﬁc or Atlantic, generally oﬀering around 18k+180k for an SMX APS South Africa to fareast. Overall, conditions in most regions remained generally weak this week. We look forward to seeing how the market performs going forward. items.parsed_text: Panam ax/Kam sarm ax Report24th March 2026 ATL: SOFTER PAC: SOFTER MID EAST: SOFTER Market Comments ATLANTIC EVENTS OF THIS WEEK HAVE BEEN DOMINATED BY MONDAY'S ANNOUNCEMENT BY THE U.S. PRESIDENT STATING "VERY GOOD AND PRODUCTIVE CONVERSATIONS REGARDING A COMPLETE AND TOTAL RESOLUTION OF OUR HOSTILITIES IN THE MIDDLE-EAST", AND A POSTPONEMENT OF MILLITARY STRIKES AGAINST IRANIAN POWER AND ENERGY INFRASTUCTURE. FOLLOWING THIS, WE SAW THE PRICE OF BRENT CRUDE PLUMMET FROM US$108.96/BARREL TO US$94.74 /BARREL WITH THE PRICE VOLATILITY CONTINUING BETWEEN US$97 TO US$100/BARREL AT TIME OF WRITING. THIS SERIES OF EVENTS IN AN ALREADY TENTATIVE ENVIRONMENT RENDERED THE MARKET ALMOST UN-TRADEABLE. WHILST IT IS NOT UNUSUAL TO HAVE SLOW MONDAYS, TRADING AND PRICING BECAME PARTICULARLY CHALLENGING DUE TO THE VOLATILE FUEL PRICES AND MOST PREFERRING TO WAIT AND SEE WHERE AND HOW PRICES MIGHT SETTLE. 1A-THE ATLANTIC BASIN DOES LOOK QUITE WELL SUPPLIED WITH A FEW PROMPT /BALLASTING SHIPS IN THE MIX, CAUSING THE MARKET TO DRIFT DOWNWARDS. IN THE NORTH WE SAW AN EARLY APRIL MINERALS STEM EX MO I RANA TO CONTINENT FIX FAIRLY QUICKLY ON VOYAGE AT BKI TC EQUIVALENT TO US$10,000/DAY. FOR LONGER GRAINS TA WE DID HEAR SEVERAL FIXING BETWEEN US$14,5/14K/DAY FOR NORTH COAST SOUTH AMERICA LOADING TO CONTINENT. IT IS FAIR TO SAY THAT A NUMBER OF THE OPEN POSITIONS HAVE SOME BACKSTOP CARGOES WHERE THEY SEEK TO OPTIMIZE ON WHICH ALLEVIATES SOME PRESSURE TO DISCOUNT SHARPLY HOWEVER THE GENERAL DIRECTION SO FAR HAS BEEN DOWNWARDS. 2A-WE HAVE SO FAR SEEN A FAIR AMOUNT OF 2A MINERALS DEMAND MOSTLY TO INDIA WHERE EARLY INTIAL BIDS STAND IN THE REGION OF US$21.5/22K/DAY FOR 70-75DAYS EX CONTINENT. WE DID HEAR A PACIFIC BALLASTER FIXING APS USG AT THE MID US$18'S + US$850KGBB. MOST OFFERS FOR 2A REMAIN CLOSER TO THE MID US$20K FOR INDIA WITH ENCOURAGEMENT FOR LESS ON LONGER DURATION GRAINS TO FAR EAST. P6-BUYING INTEREST HERE REMAINS IN THE DOLDRUMS AND THE TONNAGE LIST LOOKS LARGELY UNCHANGED DUE TO THE LONG PERIOD OF SLOW ACTIVITY. MUCH OF THE BUYING INTEREST CONTINUES TO BE DONE ON VOYAGE BASIS WHILE WE SEE INCREASINGLY OWNERS REDUCING THEIR TC OFFERS IN AN EFFORT TO DRAW CHTRS BACK TO THE TABLE. MUCH OF THE TC ENQUIRY SEEMS TO BE FROM 10TH APRIL ONWARDS WITH A GREATER CONCENTRATION FROM 20TH APRIL BUT THE TONNAGE LIST STILL HAS CONSIDERABLE LENGTH FOR EARLIER ETA'S CAUSING THE MARKET TO FEEL UNDER PRESSURE IN THE MEANTIME. INDEX MONDAY 1A 13,600 // 2A 23,500 // P6 16,756 TUESDAY 1A 13,255 // 2A 23,241 // P6 16,367 PACIFIC WE BEGAN THIS WEEK WITH FUNDAMENTALS SHAKY. IN THE NORTH, WHILST NOPAC GRAINS DEMAND REMAINS CONSISTENT, TONNAGE HAS BEEN GROWING LENGTHIER, LEADING TO BIDS DECREASING TO 16’S- 17K P3 EQUIVALENT WHILE OFFERS HOVER AROUND 19-20K’S P3 EQUIVALENT AND A FEW NOPAC FIXTURES HAVE BEEN CONCLUDED AROUND 18K P3 EQUIVALENT THUS FAR. MOVING SOUTHWARDS, AUSSIE LACKS FIRM AND SUFFICIENT DEMAND ON THE WHOLE WHILST AUS/S.CHINA COAL NOTABLY REMAINS MUTED. INDO HAS BEEN ACTIVE WITH SHIPS WITHIN 15 YEARS FIXING AT LEVELS MUCH BETTER THAN THE FATE OF THE OA SHIPS AS INDO/S.CHINA REMAINS WEAK. A DECENT LME EX S.CHINA EARLY APRIL FETCHED 16K FOR INDO/MALAYSIA, IN CONTRAST TO AN OVERAGED LME EX SCHINA END MAR WHICH FIXED LOW 12K FOR INDO/SCHINA. Asian production fell 1.9% to 104.9 Mt, following a decline in Chinese (-3.6% to 76.1 Mt) output, though Indian production climbed 7.7% to 13.6 Mt. Meanwhile, African and North American production lifted 4.6% and 3.0% to a respective 2.0 Mt and 7.4 Mt. Canadian Iron Ore Exports After recording a 6.3 Mt year-on-year increase to 62.9 Mt in 2025, Canadian iron ore exports eased 0.1 Mt from last year to 4.1 Mt in January, Canadian customs data show. The January decline included a drop in shipments to Belgium (-0.3 Mt to 0.1 Mt), Germany (-0.2 Mt to 0.2 Mt) and the Netherlands (-0.1 Mt to 0.6 Mt). Conversely, exports rose to France (+0.1 Mt to 0.6 Mt) and South Korea (+0.3 Mt to 0.5 Mt), while those to China and Japan remained steady at 0.4 Mt and 1.2 Mt, respectively. Trading Commentary Cape Routes The c5 market ticked up quite a bit on open, with just over 600kt clearing. The april traded up to 11.95, the may was paid up to 12.15 and july traded at 11.85. The back end also ticked up with q3 trading at 11.80 as q1'27 was paid up to 9.75. The c3 remained fairly quiet with the only trade reported being the april contract at 31.00. Cape The Cape FFA curve continued to lose value today in response to a weaker physical market. Liquidity for the March contract thinned as expected, with 22750 printing. Pressure on the Apr continued to mount leading to 24750 sold, from a high of 25750, while the Apr v May spread widened and weakened down to -2750. The range on May was 27250-28100 and Jun 27150-27600, with the May v Jun trading +200. Q2 was trading between 26250 and 27100, the Q2 v Q3 spread traded +550 and Q234 down to 26250. The Cal27 range was 23800-24000 and Cal28 22600-22750. PMX PMX opened lower than yesterday’s close and the weaker trend followed through the day, with selling pressure seen across the curve. Apr traded from 17750 to 16600, while May moved lower from 18000 to 17650. Jun decreased from 18000 to 17600, with Q2 going from 17900 to 17400. Q3 went from 17300 to 17000, while Q4 traded 16250 to 16000. Q2v3 spread contracted from trading 600 in the morning to 300 being hit in the afternoon. Q234 saw very little activity, trading once at 16750, and Cal 27 moved lower from 14150 to 14050. Overall, the market stayed under pressure throughout the day, with the downward move continuing into the close. SMX + HANDY A steady day of better oﬀers for SMX paper as we closed a couple hundred dollars oﬀ opening levels on quite a thinly traded day all. Apr opened the trading at $13650, closing down $325 for the day at $13375.May traded down to lows of $14150 and closing slightly oﬀ the lows at $14175. Q2 was the highlight of the day for volume with over 1400 lots traded, with most of the activity between $14150-14200, before trading down to lows of $13900, closing at $14000. Q3 traded $15200 down to $14950. Cal27 closed at ﬂat to open levels at $12400, with lows of $12350. Handy FFA, apr printed $12550, closing slightly oﬀ the lows at $12600.
